descriptors.R: nominee of the party that held the presidency from 1921 to 1933
descriptors.D: nominee of the party in office since 1933, renominating the sitting President for a third term

compile_desc.R: the party that held the presidency from 1921 to 1933

others_line: Other candidates on some ballots, including a Socialist, a Prohibition and a Communist nominee (answer "other").
never_name: Willkie, Roosevelt, McNary, Wallace, Garner, Norman Thomas, Browder, Dewey, Robert Taft or Hoover

slice_sources.men: 1940 census (April, the first to recode Mexican-origin people as white and to tabulate citizenship for all foreign-born) aged to November 1940; men 21+ outside the eleven Southern states, citizens only, American Indians included as citizens since 1924; Black voters here vote heavily Democratic since 1936; calibrated to certified 1940 returns.
slice_sources.women: 1940 census aged to November 1940, women 21+ outside the South, all enfranchised by the Nineteenth Amendment; turnout from the carried-forward women-to-men ratio, calibrated to each state's 1940 vote.
slice_sources.south-white: 1940 census aged to November 1940, white adults (now including Mexican-origin adults) in the eleven former Confederate states; poll taxes remain in eight (North Carolina, Louisiana and Florida have repealed theirs); calibrated to certified 1940 returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1940 census aged to November 1940, Black adults in the eleven former Confederate states; disfranchisement by poll tax, literacy test and the white primary continues, so the shortfall against white turnout is counted as exclusion; the few who vote lean Democratic since 1936.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1940 census aged to November 1940, foreign-born white adults who were not naturalized; no state let aliens vote.

masks: the nominee of the party out of power
a rival for the out-party nomination
